context: Small multiples data visualization — 12 monthly panels showing daily energy consumption with three years overlaid as line series in a 4x3 grid
first_impression: Clean and competent small multiples layout with deliberate palette and good structural choices, but the three overlapping noisy lines per panel make year-to-year comparison difficult to extract
what_works: Tol color palette (blue/red/green) is a principled, accessible choice over schemeCategory10, and the shared-axes approach — Y-axis only on the left column, X-axis only on the bottom row — significantly reduces clutter and follows small multiples best practices; the descriptive subtitle ('winter heating and summer AC create the seasonal U-shape') earns its place
what_doesnt: Three overlapping jagged lines with daily noise make it nearly impossible to compare years within any panel — the data encoding works against the stated insight; the crosshair interaction syncs across all 12 panels which is a nice idea, but tooltip positioning logic has a bug (the hoverMonth variable is unused) meaning tooltip content may not reliably reflect the hovered panel
